Waves, directed by Trey Edward Shults, is an emotional family drama that unfolds in two distinct parts. Set in South Florida, the first half follows Tyler (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), a high school wrestler under intense pressure, whose choices lead to life changing consequences. The second half shifts to his younger sister Emily (Taylor Russell), as she deals with grief and tries to rebuild her life.

The film stands out for its style as much as its story. Shot on 35mm by cinematographer Drew Daniels, it uses long takes, handheld movement, and natural light to keep things feeling close and personal. The visuals even change tone as the story shifts, moving from warm, vibrant colors to something cooler and more muted.

The soundtrack, featuring work by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross alongside artists like Frank Ocean and Kendrick Lamar, plays a huge role in shaping the film’s mood.

Premiering at the Telluride Film Festival in 2019, Waves was praised for its emotional intensity and structure, with Taylor Russell earning major recognition for her performance. At its core, it’s about how one moment can ripple through a family, and how people find a way to keep going afterward.
